clue.text: Protested about a particular silk

definitions.meaning: to sit in, or stage a sit-in, is to protest by occupying a place
a glossy fabric traditionally woven from silk

explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth lustrous weave, classically of silk, while staging a sit-in is a form of protest.

clue.text: Connect a non-drinker with a place of worship

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, someone who does not drink alcohol
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A temperance campaigner is linked up with a local chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is short for teetotal, describing someone who never drinks alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach things is to join or fasten them together, a synonym of connect.

clue.text: Statesman developed in camera

indicators.note: photographs are developed, and here the letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician's film was processed inside the camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges the letters of IN CAMERA. 'Statesman' is read as a man of the States, a citizen of the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the United States is a States man, a playful reading of the word for a politician.

clue.text: Engross one set of Frenchmen with Irish Gaelic

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
MM abbreviates Messieurs, the French plural of Monsieur
Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: Absorb a lone person, a group of Frenchmen and some Irish Gaelic.
explanation.walkthrough: MM is the abbreviation for Messieurs, 'gentlemen' in French.
explanation.definitionFit: To engross someone is to absorb them completely, as being plunged deep into something does.

clue.text: Alice and Mab become friendly

indicators.note: the two names transform into something else, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two girls, Alice and Mab, turn into good pals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' tells you the letters of ALICE and MAB together turn into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable describes relations marked by goodwill, a close synonym of friendly.

clue.text: When canvas worker became an attacker

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a sail is made of canvas, and canvas can mean the sails of a ship
the ant is the crossword's standard worker, from worker ants

explanation.surface: A sailmaker turned violent and became an assailant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canvas' stands for SAIL, as sailors speak of a ship being 'under canvas'.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is someone who assaults another person, the same as an attacker.

clue.text: Christmas entertainment I'm eager to begin after quiet worker gets honour

indicators.note: the remaining pieces are placed following the earlier ones

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
the ant is the crossword's standard worker
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word eager is used

explanation.surface: A cheerful person eager to start a holiday show after a silent labourer is decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour. 'after' sets the opening of 'eager' and its partner behind the quiet worker's pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomime is the traditional British family stage show staged over the festive season.

clue.text: Gather when mother's inside

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other here

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as the sun set'
ma is mother, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: People come together while Mum is indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places the mother piece within the word for when; 'gather' here is a verb, collect up.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to accumulate or collect together, just as to gather does.

clue.text: A pot of marmalade, perhaps, partly open

parts.note: marmalade is sold in a glass pot, a jar

explanation.surface: A breakfast preserve's container has its lid half off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shows a marmalade pot is just one example of a jar.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open is said to be ajar.

clue.text: She's a good bird! Quarrel with that!

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, so she is Di, and the 's adds an S
a ree is a female ruff, a wading bird

explanation.surface: Someone praises a woman as a fine bird, and a listener objects.
explanation.walkthrough: REE, the female of the ruff, is a crossword staple. 'bird' is also British slang for a woman, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute or argue against a statement is to take issue with it, a direct verb phrase.

clue.text: Couple of chaps join forces to find the dog

parts.note: Jack is a man's name
Al is a man's name, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: Two men team up to track down a hound.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'couple of chaps' are two men's names, JACK and AL, joined together.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackal is a wild canine of Africa and Asia, a member of the wider dog family.

clue.text: Smart part of church I congregate in

indicators.note: says the letters lie within the run of words church I congregate

explanation.surface: A stylish section of the church where I gather with others.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across churCH I Congregate.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and fashionable, a sense of smart describing dress.

clue.text: Scratch around for game

definitions.meaning: to grope or ... is to scratch about with hands or claws
a word board game using lettered tiles

explanation.definitionFit: To scrabble is to scrape about frantically, and the same word names a well-known tile word game.

clue.text: After preparation, points to the recipient

indicators.note: the compass letters come following the earlier piece

parts.note: in golf, address is the preparatory stance before striking the ball
E is east, so two compass points give EE

explanation.surface: Once everything is ready, someone gestures toward the person receiving the parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: A golfer's address is the set-up taken before a swing. 'After' places EE, two eastern compass points, behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: An addressee is the person a letter or parcel is directed to, and so receives it.

clue.text: Loving a party band

parts.note: a do is an informal party
a ring is a circular band, as worn on a finger

explanation.surface: Fond of a celebration and the group playing at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' is a ring of metal, not a group of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoring means showing deep affection, a close synonym of loving.

clue.text: Could this be the response from 20?

indicators.note: asks whether the letters of the other entry might be rearranged into this one

parts.note: the number points to the answer of 20 across

explanation.surface: A question about whether a reply came from clue 20.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could this be' signals that 16 and 20 are anagrams of each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction is a reply or answer prompted by something, the same as a response.

clue.text: Beatles' early location has special chambers

parts.note: the Cavern Club in Liverpool where the band played many early gigs

explanation.surface: The Beatles' first venue boasts unique rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cavern Club is a Liverpool cellar venue where the Beatles played early in their career.
explanation.definitionFit: Caverns are large underground hollows, and chambers can mean natural cavities.

clue.text: Desire of a prince with a small, French, female

parts.note: petite is the French word for small in its feminine form

explanation.surface: A royal longs for a tiny French woman.
explanation.walkthrough: PETITE is French 'small' with the feminine ending, which is why 'female' is included.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetite is a craving or hunger for something, the same as a desire.

clue.text: Made certain of being safe in the end

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: end taken in its plain sense of a conclusion
sure can mean safe, as in a sure bet or sure footing

explanation.surface: Someone checked that all would be secure at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' splits 'the end' to take the word for safe; 'of being' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to guarantee or make sure, so the past form means made certain.

clue.text: Could this be made from 16?

indicators.note: asks whether this entry might be built by rearranging the letters of the other one

parts.note: the number points to the answer of 16 down

explanation.surface: A question about whether something could be made from clue 16.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be made from' says the letters of 16 are reworked; the answer, something made, is also what the whole clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A creation is anything brought into being or produced, so it is a thing made.

clue.text: Illinois's former shrub

parts.note: IL is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Illinois
ex means former, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: A plant that used to grow in Illinois.
explanation.walkthrough: IL is the US postal code for Illinois.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the botanical genus of holly, an evergreen bush.

clue.text: Put forward poles or south Europeans first

indicators.note: says to take the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Ask whether Poles or southern Europeans should lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes the first letters of 'poles or south Europeans'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pose a question is to raise or propose it for consideration.

clue.text: Puny person's bright pink

definitions.meaning: an informal term for a small, weak person
a vivid pink colour named after the crustacean

explanation.definitionFit: The small crustacean lends its name both to a weedy little person and to a vivid pinkish colour.

clue.text: Grand lady of pinched appearance

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
an aunt is a female relative, a lady of the family

explanation.surface: A great dame looks drawn and thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' gives G and 'lady' gives AUNT, a female relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaunt describes someone thin and haggard, with a drawn, hollow face.

clue.text: Fly set spinning twice

indicators.note: the rearranged letters appear two times in a row
the word set is twirled around so its letters fall in a new order

explanation.surface: An insect is twice sent whirling round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' rearranges SET to TSE, and 'twice' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African blood-sucking insect that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Loosen head, turn it the other way

indicators.note: says the words head and turn are turned about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to slacken one's head by twisting it in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other way' rearranges the letters of HEAD and TURN together; 'it' just links them.
explanation.definitionFit: To unthread is to draw the thread out of something, loosening it.

clue.text: Drank hard after returning to military stores

indicators.note: the word for heavy drinking is read backwards

parts.note: to tope is to drink alcohol heavily, so toped is drank hard

explanation.surface: A soldier drank heavily on returning to the supply base.
explanation.walkthrough: TOPED, from the old verb 'tope', drink to excess, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storehouse, especially for military supplies and equipment.

clue.text: Judgement conveyed to independent soldiers finally caught

parts.note: sent means conveyed or dispatched
men is a common word for soldiers

indicators.note: takes only the last letter of the word caught

explanation.surface: A verdict is delivered to freelance troops who were at last captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives the T of 'caught'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment can mean an opinion or view, the same as a judgement.
